sanskrit: saumadattiṃ raṇe śūram ārśyaśṛṅgiṃ ca rākṣasam trigartarājaṃ ca raṇe saha sarvair mahārathaiḥ aham āvārayiṣyāmi veleva makarālayam
english: Saumadatti, the hero in battle, and Ārśyaśṛṅgi the rākṣasa, and the king of the Trigartas in the fray, together with all their great chariot-warriors—these I shall hold back, as the shore holds back the abode of sea-monsters.

sanskrit: kurūṃś ca sahitān sarvān ye caiṣāṃ sainikāḥ sthitāḥ nivārayiṣyāmi raṇe sādhayasva pitāmaham
english: And all the Kurus assembled, and whatever soldiers of theirs stand ready, I shall ward off in the battle; do you go after the grandsire.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ śikhaṇḍī gāṅgeyam abhyadhāvat pitāmaham pāñcālyaḥ samare kruddho dharmātmānaṃ yatavratam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How did Śikhaṇḍin, the Pāñcāla, enraged in battle, rush upon the son of Gaṅgā, the grandsire, that righteous soul of steadfast vows?

sanskrit: ke 'rakṣan pāṇḍavānīke śikhaṇḍinam udāyudham tvaramāṇās tvarākāle jigīṣanto mahārathāḥ
english: Who among the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍava host, hastening in the hour of haste and eager for victory, guarded Śikhaṇḍin as he raised his weapon?

sanskrit: kathaṃ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmaḥ sa tasmin daśame 'hani ayudhyata mahāvīryaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ sahasṛñjayaiḥ
english: How did Bhīṣma, son of Śāntanu, that mighty hero, fight on that tenth day against the Pāṇḍavas together with the Sṛñjayas?

sanskrit: na mṛṣyāmi raṇe bhīṣmaṃ pratyudyātaṃ śikhaṇḍinam kaccin na rathabhaṅgo 'sya dhanur vāśīryatāsyataḥ
english: I cannot bear that Bhīṣma in battle was confronted by Śikhaṇḍin coming against him. Surely there was no breaking of his chariot, nor did his bow shatter as he shot?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca nāśīryata dhanus tasya rathabhaṅgo na cāpy abhūt yudhyamānasya saṃgrāme bhīṣmasya bharatarṣabha nighnataḥ samare śatrūñ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: His bow did not shatter, nor was there any breaking of his chariot, O bull of the Bhāratas, while Bhīṣma fought in the engagement, slaying his foes in battle with arrows whose joints were well bent.

sanskrit: anekaśatasāhasrās tāvakānāṃ mahārathāḥ rathadantigaṇā rājan hayāś caiva susajjitāḥ abhyavartanta yuddhāya puraskṛtya pitāmaham
english: Many hundreds of thousands of your great chariot-warriors, O king, with their throngs of chariots and elephants and their well-caparisoned horses, advanced to battle, placing the grandsire at their head.

sanskrit: yathāpratijñaṃ kauravya sa cāpi samitiṃjayaḥ pārthānām akarod bhīṣmaḥ satataṃ samitikṣayam
english: True to his vow, O Kaurava, Bhīṣma the conqueror in assemblies wrought a ceaseless slaughter among the hosts of the Pārthas.

sanskrit: yudhyamānaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ vinighnantaṃ parāñ śaraiḥ pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ sarva evābhyavārayan
english: As that great archer fought, striking down his enemies with arrows, the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas, one and all, sought to ward him off.

sanskrit: daśame 'hani saṃprāpte tatāpa ripuvāhinīm kīryamāṇāṃ śitair bāṇaiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: When the tenth day had come, he scorched the army of his foes, strewing it with whetted shafts by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: na hi bhīṣmaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ pāṇḍavāḥ pāṇḍupūrvaja aśaknuvan raṇe jetuṃ pāśahastam ivāntakam
english: For the Pāṇḍavas, O ancestor of Pāṇḍu's line, were unable to vanquish in battle the great archer Bhīṣma, who was like Death with noose in hand.

sanskrit: athopāyān mahārāja savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ trāsayan rathinaḥ sarvān bībhatsur aparājitaḥ
english: Then, O great king, Savyasācin the scorcher of foes came forward, the unconquered Bībhatsu, terrifying all the chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: siṃhavad vinadann uccair dhanurjyāṃ vikṣipan muhuḥ śaraughān visṛjan pārtho vyacarat kālavad raṇe
english: Roaring aloud like a lion, twanging his bowstring again and again, loosing floods of arrows, the Pārtha ranged through the battle like Time itself.

sanskrit: tasya śabdena vitrastās tāvakā bharatarṣabha siṃhasyeva mṛgā rājan vyadravanta mahābhayāt
english: Terrified by his roar, O bull of the Bhāratas, your men fled in great fear, O king, like deer before a lion.

sanskrit: jayantaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ dṛṣṭvā tvatsainyaṃ cābhipīḍitam duryodhanas tato bhīṣmam abravīd bhṛśapīḍitaḥ
english: Seeing the Pāṇḍava triumphant and your army hard pressed, Duryodhana, himself sorely afflicted, then spoke to Bhīṣma:

sanskrit: eṣa pāṇḍusutas tāta śvetāśvaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ dahate māmakān sarvān kṛṣṇavartmeva kānanam
english: "This son of Pāṇḍu, father, with his white horses and Kṛṣṇa for his charioteer, consumes all my men as fire, whose path is black, consumes a forest.

sanskrit: paśya sainyāni gāṅgeya dravamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ pāṇḍavena yudhāṃ śreṣṭha kālyamānāni saṃyuge
english: Behold, O son of Gaṅgā, the armies fleeing in every direction, driven off in the conflict, O best of warriors, by the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: yathā paśugaṇān pālaḥ saṃkālayati kānane tathedaṃ māmakaṃ sainyaṃ kālyate śatrutāpana
english: As a herdsman drives his herds of cattle through the forest, so is this army of mine driven, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayaśarair bhagnaṃ dravamāṇam itas tataḥ bhīmo hy eṣa durādharṣo vidrāvayati me balam
english: Broken by Dhanaṃjaya's arrows, it flees this way and that; and this irresistible Bhīma scatters my forces.

sanskrit: sātyakiś cekitānaś ca mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau abhimanyuś ca vikrānto vāhinīṃ dahate mama
english: Sātyaki and Cekitāna and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī, and valiant Abhimanyu—they burn up my host.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tathā śūro rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ vyadrāvayetāṃ sahasā sainyaṃ mama mahābalau
english: And the hero Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, those two of mighty strength, have suddenly put my army to flight.

sanskrit: vadhyamānasya sainyasya sarvair etair mahābalaiḥ nānyāṃ gatiṃ prapaśyāmi sthāne yuddhe ca bhārata
english: For this army, slaughtered by all these mighty ones, I see no other refuge to hold its ground and fight, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: ṛte tvāṃ puruṣavyāghra devatulyaparākrama paryāptaś ca bhavān kṣipraṃ pīḍitānāṃ gatir bhava
english: save you, O tiger among men, whose prowess equals the gods'. You are equal to the task—be swiftly the refuge of the afflicted!"

sanskrit: evam ukto mahārāja pitā devavratas tava cintayitvā muhūrtaṃ tu kṛtvā niścayam ātmanaḥ tava saṃdhārayan putram abravīc chaṃtanoḥ sutaḥ
english: Thus addressed, O great king, your father Devavrata, son of Śāntanu, having pondered a moment and made his resolve within himself, spoke to your son to steady him:

sanskrit: duryodhana vijānīhi sthiro bhava viśāṃ pate pūrvakālaṃ tava mayā pratijñātaṃ mahābala
english: "Duryodhana, understand this and be steadfast, O lord of peoples. Long ago I made a vow to you, O mighty one:

sanskrit: hatvā daśa sahasrāṇi kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahātmanām saṃgrāmād vyapayātavyam etat karma mamāhnikam iti tat kṛtavāṃś cāhaṃ yathoktaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: that having slain ten thousand of the great-souled warriors I would withdraw from the field—this was to be my daily task; and that, O bull of the Bhāratas, I have done as I promised.

sanskrit: adya cāpi mahat karma prakariṣye mahāhave ahaṃ vā nihataḥ śeṣye haniṣye vādya pāṇḍavān
english: Today too I shall perform a mighty deed in the great battle: either I shall lie slain, or I shall slay the Pāṇḍavas this day.

sanskrit: adya te puruṣavyāghra pratimokṣye ṛṇaṃ mahat bhartṛpiṇḍakṛtaṃ rājan nihataḥ pṛtanāmukhe
english: This day, O tiger among men, I shall discharge the great debt I owe for my master's bread, O king, by falling slain at the head of the host."

sanskrit: ity uktvā bharataśreṣṭhaḥ kṣatriyān pratapañ śaraiḥ āsasāda durādharṣaḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: Having spoken thus, that best of the Bhāratas, irresistible, scorching the warriors with his arrows, fell upon the army of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: anīkamadhye tiṣṭhantaṃ gāṅgeyaṃ bharatarṣabha āśīviṣam iva kruddhaṃ pāṇḍavāḥ paryavārayan
english: As the son of Gaṅgā stood in the midst of the host, O bull of the Bhāratas, wrathful like a venomous serpent, the Pāṇḍavas surrounded him on every side.

sanskrit: daśame 'hani tasmiṃs tu darśayañ śaktim ātmanaḥ rājañ śatasahasrāṇi so 'vadhīt kurunandana
english: But on that tenth day, displaying his own might, O king, O joy of the Kurus, he slew hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: pañcālānāṃ ca ye śreṣṭhā rājaputrā mahābalāḥ teṣām ādatta tejāṃsi jalaṃ sūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ
english: And of those mighty princes who were the foremost of the Pāñcālas, he drank up the splendor, as the sun with its rays drinks up water.

sanskrit: hatvā daśa sahasrāṇi kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām sārohāṇāṃ mahārāja hayānāṃ cāyutaṃ punaḥ
english: Having slain ten thousand swift elephants with their riders, O great king, and ten thousand horses besides,

sanskrit: pūrṇe śatasahasre dve padātīnāṃ narottamaḥ prajajvāla raṇe bhīṣmo vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: and full two hundred thousand foot-soldiers, that best of men, Bhīṣma, blazed forth in the battle like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: na cainaṃ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ ke cic chekur nirīkṣitum uttaraṃ mārgam āsthāya tapantam iva bhāskaram
english: And none among the Pāṇḍavas could even look upon him, as upon the sun blazing when it has entered the northern path.

sanskrit: te pāṇḍaveyāḥ saṃrabdhā maheṣvāsena pīḍitāḥ vadhāyābhyadravan bhīṣmaṃ sṛñjayāś ca mahārathāḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas, enraged and afflicted by that great archer, together with the Sṛñjaya chariot-warriors, rushed upon Bhīṣma to slay him.

sanskrit: sa yudhyamāno bahubhir bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas tadā avakīrṇo mahābāhuḥ śailo meghair ivāsitaiḥ
english: As he fought against the many, Bhīṣma, son of Śāntanu, that mighty-armed one, was then covered over like a mountain by dark clouds.

sanskrit: putrās tu tava gāṅgeyaṃ samantāt paryavārayan mahatyā senayā sārdhaṃ tato yuddham avartata
english: But your sons, with a great army, surrounded the son of Gaṅgā on every side; and thereupon the battle was joined.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca arjunas tu raṇe rājan dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmasya vikramam śikhaṇḍinam athovāca samabhyehi pitāmaham
english: Saṃjaya said: But Arjuna, O king, seeing Bhīṣma's prowess in the battle, then said to Śikhaṇḍin: "Go forth against the grandsire.

sanskrit: na cāpi bhīs tvayā kāryā bhīṣmād adya kathaṃ cana aham enaṃ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ pātayiṣye rathottamāt
english: And no fear at all need you feel of Bhīṣma this day; I shall bring him down from his splendid chariot with my sharp arrows."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu pārthena śikhaṇḍī bharatarṣabha abhyadravata gāṅgeyaṃ śrutvā pārthasya bhāṣitam
english: Thus addressed by the Pārtha, O bull of the Bhāratas, Śikhaṇḍin, hearing the Pārtha's words, charged upon the son of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tathā rājan saubhadraś ca mahārathaḥ hṛṣṭāv ādravatāṃ bhīṣmaṃ śrutvā pārthasya bhāṣitam
english: So too, O king, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and the son of Subhadrā, that great chariot-warrior, hearing the Pārtha's words, rushed gladly upon Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: virāṭadrupadau vṛddhau kuntibhojaś ca daṃśitaḥ abhyadravata gāṅgeyaṃ putrasya tava paśyataḥ
english: The aged Virāṭa and Drupada, and Kuntibhoja in his armor, charged upon the son of Gaṅgā while your son looked on.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca dharmarājaś ca vīryavān tathetarāṇi sainyāni sarvāṇy eva viśāṃ pate samādravanta gāṅgeyaṃ śrutvā pārthasya bhāṣitam
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, and the valiant King of Righteousness, and all the other armies as well, O lord of peoples, hearing the Pārtha's words, rushed together upon the son of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: pratyudyayus tāvakāś ca sametās tān mahārathān yathāśakti yathotsāhaṃ tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: And your warriors, assembled, advanced to meet those great chariot-warriors, each to the best of his strength and ardor; hear me as I recount it.

sanskrit: citraseno mahārāja cekitānaṃ samabhyayāt bhīṣmaprepsuṃ raṇe yāntaṃ vṛṣaṃ vyāghraśiśur yathā
english: Citrasena, O great king, advanced against Cekitāna, who was moving in the battle eager to reach Bhīṣma, as a tiger-cub goes against a bull.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ mahārāja bhīṣmāntikam upāgatam tvaramāṇo raṇe yattaṃ kṛtavarmā nyavārayat
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, as he came near to Bhīṣma, intent and hastening in the battle, was checked by Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ susaṃkruddhaṃ gāṅgeyasya vadhaiṣiṇam tvaramāṇo mahārāja saumadattir nyavārayat
english: Bhīmasena, in great wrath and seeking the slaying of the son of Gaṅgā, was checked in haste, O great king, by Saumadatti.

sanskrit: tathaiva nakulaṃ vīraṃ kirantaṃ sāyakān bahūn vikarṇo vārayām āsa icchan bhīṣmasya jīvitam
english: Likewise the hero Nakula, scattering his many shafts, Vikarṇa warded off, desiring to save Bhīṣma's life.

sanskrit: sahadevaṃ tathā yāntaṃ yattaṃ bhīṣmarathaṃ prati vārayām āsa saṃkruddhaḥ kṛpaḥ śāradvato yudhi
english: And Sahadeva, as he pressed intent toward Bhīṣma's chariot, Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat, enraged, warded off in the fight.

sanskrit: rākṣasaṃ krūrakarmāṇaṃ bhaimaseniṃ mahābalam bhīṣmasya nidhanaṃ prepsuṃ durmukho 'bhyadravad balī
english: Against the rākṣasa of cruel deeds, the son of Bhīmasena, mighty in strength and eager for Bhīṣma's death, the strong Durmukha charged.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ samare kruddham ārśyaśṛṅgir avārayat abhimanyuṃ mahārāja yāntaṃ bhīṣmarathaṃ prati sudakṣiṇo mahārāja kāmbojaḥ pratyavārayat
english: Sātyaki, wrathful in the battle, Ārśyaśṛṅgi warded off; and Abhimanyu, O great king, as he advanced toward Bhīṣma's chariot, Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja, O great king, turned back.

sanskrit: virāṭadrupadau vṛddhau sametāv arimardanau aśvatthāmā tataḥ kruddho vārayām āsa bhārata
english: The aged Virāṭa and Drupada, those two crushers of foes joined together, Aśvatthāman then in wrath held off, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tathā pāṇḍusutaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhīṣmasya vadhakāṅkṣiṇam bhāradvājo raṇe yatto dharmaputram avārayat
english: So too the eldest son of Pāṇḍu, who longed for Bhīṣma's slaying, the son of Bharadvāja, intent in the battle, held off—the son of Dharma.

sanskrit: arjunaṃ rabhasaṃ yuddhe puraskṛtya śikhaṇḍinam bhīṣmaprepsuṃ mahārāja tāpayantaṃ diśo daśa duḥśāsano maheṣvāso vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Arjuna, impetuous in the fight, with Śikhaṇḍin placed before him, eager to reach Bhīṣma and scorching the ten directions, O great king, Duḥśāsana the great archer warded off in the engagement.

sanskrit: anye ca tāvakā yodhāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathān bhīṣmāyābhimukhaṃ yātān vārayām āsur āhave
english: And other warriors of yours warded off in the battle the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas as they advanced toward Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu sainyāni prākrośata punaḥ punaḥ abhidravata saṃrabdhā bhīṣmam ekaṃ mahābalam
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna cried out to the armies again and again: "Rush in fury upon Bhīṣma alone, the mighty one!

sanskrit: eṣo 'rjuno raṇe bhīṣmaṃ prayāti kurunandanaḥ abhidravata mā bhaiṣṭa bhīṣmo na prāpsyate hi vaḥ
english: This Arjuna, joy of the Kurus, advances in the battle against Bhīṣma. Rush in, fear not; for Bhīṣma shall not reach you.

sanskrit: arjunaṃ samare yoddhuṃ notsahetāpi vāsavaḥ kim u bhīṣmo raṇe vīrā gatasattvo 'lpajīvitaḥ
english: Not even Vāsava would dare to fight Arjuna in battle—how much less Bhīṣma, O heroes, whose strength is spent and whose life is short!"

sanskrit: iti senāpateḥ śrutvā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ abhyadravanta saṃhṛṣṭā gāṅgeyasya rathaṃ prati
english: Hearing this from their commander, the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas rushed forward, delighted, toward the chariot of the son of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: āgacchatas tān samare vāryoghān prabalān iva nyavārayanta saṃhṛṣṭās tāvakāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: As they came on in the battle like mighty floods of water, your bulls among men, delighted, held them back.

sanskrit: duḥśāsano mahārāja bhayaṃ tyaktvā mahārathaḥ bhīṣmasya jīvitākāṅkṣī dhanaṃjayam upādravat
english: Duḥśāsana, O great king, that great chariot-warrior, casting off fear and longing to save Bhīṣma's life, rushed upon Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ śūrā gāṅgeyasya rathaṃ prati abhyadravanta saṃgrāme tava putrān mahārathān
english: Likewise the heroic Pāṇḍavas rushed in the engagement toward the chariot of the son of Gaṅgā, against your sons, the great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma citrarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate duḥśāsanarathaṃ prāpto yat pārtho nātyavartata
english: There we beheld a marvel of wondrous form, O lord of peoples: that the Pārtha, having reached Duḥśāsana's chariot, could not pass beyond it.

sanskrit: yathā vārayate velā kṣubhitaṃ vai mahārṇavam tathaiva pāṇḍavaṃ kruddhaṃ tava putro nyavārayat
english: As the shore holds back the turbulent great ocean, so did your son hold back the wrathful Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: ubhau hi rathināṃ śreṣṭhāv ubhau bhārata durjayau ubhau candrārkasadṛśau kāntyā dīptyā ca bhārata
english: For both were the foremost of chariot-warriors, both hard to conquer, O Bhārata; both were like the moon and the sun in beauty and in radiance, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tau tathā jātasaṃrambhāv anyonyavadhakāṅkṣiṇau samīyatur mahāsaṃkhye mayaśakrau yathā purā
english: Both thus roused to fury, each longing for the other's death, they met in the great battle as Maya and Śakra met of old.

sanskrit: duḥśāsano mahārāja pāṇḍavaṃ viśikhais tribhiḥ vāsudevaṃ ca viṃśatyā tāḍayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Duḥśāsana, O great king, struck the Pāṇḍava with three shafts and Vāsudeva with twenty in the engagement.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno jātamanyur vārṣṇeyaṃ vīkṣya pīḍitam duḥśāsanaṃ śatenājau nārācānāṃ samārpayat te tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā papuḥ śoṇitam āhave
english: Then Arjuna, his anger kindled at the sight of the Vārṣṇeya struck, pierced Duḥśāsana in the fight with a hundred iron shafts; and they, cleaving his armor, drank his blood in the battle.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tataḥ kruddhaḥ pārthaṃ vivyādha pañcabhiḥ lalāṭe bharataśreṣṭha śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Then Duḥśāsana in wrath pierced the Pārtha in the forehead with five arrows whose joints were well bent, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: lalāṭasthais tu tair bāṇaiḥ śuśubhe pāṇḍavottamaḥ yathā merur mahārāja śṛṅgair atyartham ucchritaiḥ
english: With those arrows set in his forehead, that best of the Pāṇḍavas shone, O great king, like Meru with its peaks towering exceedingly high.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsaḥ putreṇa tava dhanvinā vyarājata raṇe pārthaḥ kiṃśukaḥ puṣpavān iva
english: Sorely pierced by your son the bowman, that great archer, the Pārtha, glowed in the battle like a kiṃśuka tree in flower.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaṃ tataḥ kruddhaḥ pīḍayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ parvaṇīva susaṃkruddho rāhur ugro niśākaram
english: Then the Pāṇḍava in wrath afflicted Duḥśāsana, as fierce Rāhu in fury afflicts the moon on the day of conjunction.

sanskrit: pīḍyamāno balavatā putras tava viśāṃ pate vivyādha samare pārthaṃ kaṅkapatraiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Hard pressed by that mighty one, your son, O lord of peoples, pierced the Pārtha in the battle with heron-feathered shafts whetted on stone.

sanskrit: tasya pārtho dhanuś chittvā tvaramāṇaḥ parākramī ājaghāna tataḥ paścāt putraṃ te navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The valiant Pārtha, swiftly cutting his bow, then struck your son thereafter with nine arrows.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya bhīṣmasya pramukhe sthitaḥ arjunaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: He, taking up another bow and standing before Bhīṣma, struck Arjuna with twenty-five shafts in the arms and on the breast.

sanskrit: tasya kruddho mahārāja pāṇḍavaḥ śatrukarśanaḥ apraiṣīd viśikhān ghorān yamadaṇḍopamān bahūn
english: Enraged at him, O great king, the Pāṇḍava, tormentor of foes, dispatched many terrible shafts like the rods of Yama.

sanskrit: aprāptān eva tān bāṇāṃś ciccheda tanayas tava yatamānasya pārthasya tad adbhutam ivābhavat pārthaṃ ca niśitair bāṇair avidhyat tanayas tava
english: Those arrows of the striving Pārtha your son cut down before they reached him—that seemed a marvel; and your son pierced the Pārtha with whetted shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho raṇe pārthaḥ śarān saṃdhāya kārmuke preṣayām āsa samare svarṇapuṅkhāñ śilāśitān
english: Then the Pārtha in wrath, fitting his arrows to the bow, loosed in the battle golden-feathered shafts whetted on stone.
